knowledges.content: The MESSAGE, AGGREGATE, and UPDATE functions of any message-passing GNN are replaced by their quaternion counterparts so that the layerwise message-passing semantics are preserved in quaternion space.
knowledges.label: claim_1

knowledges.content: Representing layer weights as quaternion matrices and grouping four real feature channels into one quaternion reduces the number of independent trainable real parameters by a factor of four relative to an equivalent real-valued GNN weight matrix.
knowledges.label: claim_2

knowledges.content: A quaternion weight mapping from $F$ real input features to $F'$ real outputs uses $F/4\times F'/4$ quaternion entries, yielding one-fourth the degrees of freedom of the corresponding real weight matrix.
knowledges.label: claim_3

knowledges.content: Quaternion matrix multiplications have the same asymptotic time complexity as the corresponding real matrix multiplications.
knowledges.label: claim_4

knowledges.content: The parameter reduction described in claim 2 is achieved without increasing matrix-multiplication time complexity. [Referenced claim 2: Representing layer weights as quaternion matrices and grouping four real feature channels into one quaternion reduces the number of independent trainable real parameters by a factor of four relative to an equivalent real-valued GNN weight matrix.]
knowledges.label: claim_5

knowledges.content: When QMPNN variants of standard GNN architectures are trained under the same hyperparameters as those standard GNN architectures and evaluated on standard datasets, the quaternion models achieve comparable or better accuracy, ROC-AUC, or Hits@K (proportion of top-K predictions that are correct) while using roughly one-fourth of the trainable parameters of those standard GNN architectures.
knowledges.label: claim_6

knowledges.content: (a) node classification on Cora: real GCN 85.2 ± 1.3 accuracy with 140.5K parameters vs QGCN 84.1 ± 1.5 accuracy with 42.1K parameters;
knowledges.label: claim_7

knowledges.content: (b) node classification on PubMed: GCN 79.1 ± 1.2 with 131.9K parameters vs QGCN 78.4 ± 1.4 with 41.7K parameters;
knowledges.label: claim_8

knowledges.content: (c) link prediction on CORA: GCN ROC-AUC 79.27 ± 0.47 with 96.0K parameters vs QGCN ROC-AUC 83.55 ± 0.03 with 27.2K parameters;
knowledges.label: claim_9

knowledges.content: (d) graph classification on MUTAG: GCN 83.54 ± 0.40 accuracy with 4.8K parameters vs QGCN 88.61 ± 0.66 accuracy with 4.4K parameters.
knowledges.label: claim_10

knowledges.content: Across all tasks and datasets evaluated, quaternion variants of standard GNN architectures frequently perform within a small margin of the corresponding real models and sometimes exceed their performance while consistently having approximately one-fourth the trainable parameter count of the corresponding real models.
knowledges.label: claim_11

knowledges.content: Winning graph-lottery tickets exist for both real-valued GNNs and QMPNNs.
knowledges.label: claim_12

knowledges.content: Magnitude-based iterative pruning identifies subnetworks that match baseline performance at sparsity levels down to approximately 1–20% of the original parameter count across multiple architectures and tasks.
knowledges.label: claim_13

knowledges.content: QMPNN variants scale to large graph datasets and maintain performance comparable to real-valued GNNs while using fewer parameters.
knowledges.label: claim_14

knowledges.content: on OGBN-Arxiv node classification, GCN achieves 72.8 ± 1.5 accuracy with 145.1K parameters versus QGCN 72.3 ± 1.6 with 43.5K parameters;
knowledges.label: claim_15

knowledges.content: on OGBG-COLLAB link prediction, QGCN achieves Hits@50 45.80 ± 1.35 with 6.4K parameters compared to GCN 44.02 ± 1.57 with 12.5K parameters.
knowledges.label: claim_16

knowledges.content: the quaternion reparameterization is effective on large-scale graph benchmarks.
knowledges.label: claim_17
